sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2019. A fragment of Papua New Guinea philology. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 37: 42-60 [journal PDF]. ISSN 0023-1959. (ANU Open Research hdl:1885/299643)
sources.note: Nothing on Pulabu. No prosodic statement for any language; the only phonetic remarks concern Maclay's transcription of Bongu (Cyrillic/German spellings). a full-text search for stress/accent over the text: 0 relevant hits.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp. doi:10.15144/PL-D30 (Pulabu = language B10)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 7 (p. vii): transcription 'rendered in a semiphonemic form'; p. viii fluctuation table has a Pulabu heading with only dashes; no mention of stress/accent/tone anywhere (note 3 p. 172 concerns Dumpu-Watiwa being tonal). B10 Pulabu forms carry aspiration, length and trill marks but no stress marks (visual check printed p. 3).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 569-612. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.2: Kabenau Family = Arawum, Kolom, Suroi, Lemio, Pulabu; 'Arawum and Pulabu are new members. Zoller's (1891) word list of Kadda belongs to the Pulabu language.' Population B10 Pulabu 116; Table I structural features (Pulabu the Rai Coast exception for object-marker suffixing). No prosody.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Department of Linguistics, Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. vi+160 pp., maps. doi:10.15144/PL-B41; hdl:1885/146484 (Pulabu = language B10, Kabenau Family, Rai Coast Stock; index 'PULABU (Kadda)')
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. The volume is a preliminary classification (phyla/stocks/families with member languages), a per-language list of villages and numbers of speakers, an index of language names and maps; the repository text (212 KB, whole book) has zero occurrences of stress, accent, tone, tonal, phonolog-, transcription or orthograph-. Pulabu appears only as Kabenau-Family member B10 with its village/population figures and the alias Kadda.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C19
sources.note: Does not cover Pulabu: ch. 2.4 lists Pulabu (68) among Bogadjim Census Division villages 'linguistically still unknown'. Its survey-wide sentence (p. 6) 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' therefore does not apply to Pulabu data.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Pulabu not named (their Kabenau Family = Kolom, Suroi, Lemio, Gurumbu, Watiwa). Sec. 6.1: 'In Suroi stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words' (sister language); nothing on Pulabu.

sources.citation: Zöller, Hugo. 1891. Deutsch-Neuguinea und meine Ersteigung des Finisterre-Gebirges. Stuttgart: Union Deutsche Verlagsgesellschaft. xxxii+546 pp. ('Kadda' wordlist, identified as Pulabu by Z'graggen 1975a)
sources.note: Only other first-hand Pulabu data in print; a 19th-century explorer's comparative wordlist, very unlikely to comment on Betonung, but not opened.

sources.citation: Zöller, Hugo. 1890. Untersuchungen über 24 Sprachen aus dem Schutzgebiet der Neuguinea-Compagnie. Petermanns Geographische Mitteilungen 36: 122-128, 145-152, 181 (Kadda among the inland Astrolabe Bay vocabularies).
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress. Method notes only: for Poom, Kadda, Elisabeth-Inseln etc. only c. 100 words were obtained; Dschongu, Mannikam, Kadda vocabularies taken inland from Astrolabe Bay with Herr Yelliott and Bongu men; Kadda dialect also spoken in several inland villages; loan percentages (Kadda 10.5% Malayo-Polynesian resemblances).

The item is Z'graggen's handwritten field notebook of the c.300-item Madang elicitation list (plus some pronoun/verb 'structural elements', cf.
